                              JORDAN JAFFE’S INITIAL BRIEF

       Mr. Jaffe submits this Initial Brief in support of Route 894, the Joint Applicants’ Proposed

Route. As demonstrated below, Route 894 not only provides a superior balance across applicable

Public Utility Regulatory Act (“PURA”) and Commission routing criteria, but it also avoids

impacts to the Cavallino Airport.


                                I.     EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

       The Commission should adopt Route 894 and reject all alternative routes that depend on

Link J33. As demonstrated below and in the testimony of Arthur D’Andrea, Route 894

outperforms the alternatives across statutory and regulatory routing criteria: it is near the shortest




                                                  2
 and least expensive of all filed routes, 1 has among the fewest habitable structures within 500 feet

of its centerline,2 and parallels compatible rights-of-way (“ROW”) for nearly 44% of its length. 3

        Beyond those affirmative merits, the routes that rely on Link J33 carry a disqualifying

defect: they threaten the operational integrity of a private use airport (the “Cavallino Airport”), a

facility the Joint Applicants’ EA entirely failed to identify despite its location well within the

10,000-foot radius the EA itself used to inventory airstrips. 4 That omission renders the EA’s

analysis of Link J33 routes materially incomplete.5 Routes using Link J33 must therefore be

treated as having one additional private airstrip conflict not reflected in the filed analysis. 6

        Considering PURA and Commission routing criteria, the Commission should select Route

894.

                                   II.      SUPPORT FOR ROUTE 894

        PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and Commission Rule § 25.101(b)(3)(B) require the Commission to

consider several factors in transmission line routing, perhaps most importantly cost, total length,

paralleling of existing compatible right-of-way (“ROW”), and the policy of prudent avoidance. 7

        As explained in the direct testimony of Mr. D’Andrea, Route 894 satisfies these criteria

better than the alternatives, achieving the best overall balance across the 122 filed routes

                                                         3
 considered in this proceeding.8 The Commission has consistently recognized in prior CCN

proceedings that no single route excels on every factor simultaneously; the task is holistic

balancing.9 On that measure, Route 894 stands out.

           1. Cost

           Route 894 carries an estimated total cost of $1,680,919,000—only 2.73% more expensive

than the least costly filed route and approximately 9.52% less costly than the most expensive filed

route.10         Within Route 894’s own geographic corridor, the 32 filed routes range from

approximately $1,658,694,000 to $1,842,214,000, and Route 894’s estimated cost of

$1,680,919,000 places it among the most cost-effective options. 11

           The Commission need not select the single lowest-cost route; modest cost differentials are

routinely justified when a route performs better on other important criteria. 12 Here, Route 894’s

marginal premium over the cheapest alternatives is more than offset by its superior performance

on length, prudent avoidance, and ROW paralleling, as discussed below. 13

           2. Length

           Route 894 is approximately 223.7 miles in length, near the shorter end of all 122 filed

routes.14 Shorter routes require less ROW acquisition, disturb less land, generate fewer potential

                                                             4
 environmental and community impacts, and result in lower long-term maintenance costs. 15 The

Commission has historically given substantial weight to route length as a proxy for cumulative

impact.16 Route 894’s near-minimum length within its corridor is a meaningful advantage over

longer alternatives.

        3. Paralleling Existing Compatible ROW and Property Lines

        Commission Rule § 25.101(b)(3)(B) expressly prefers routes that parallel or utilize existing

compatible ROW—including existing transmission lines, public roads and highways, railroads,

and apparent property lines.17 Paralleling existing corridors concentrates land use impacts in areas

already burdened by other infrastructure, reduces visual intrusion on productive agricultural and

ranch land, and minimizes the footprint of new easement acquisition. 18

        Route 894 parallels existing compatible ROW or apparent property boundaries for

approximately 43.9% of its length.19 This is among the highest percentages of any filed route,

which range from 29.1% to 50.6%, placing Route 894 in the upper tier of performance on this

criterion.20

        4. Habitable Structures & Prudent Avoidance

        Prudent avoidance, or the policy of “limiting exposures to electric and magnetic fields that

can be avoided with reasonable investments of money and effort,” is a particularly significant

       20

 criterion in this proceeding given the wide disparity among filed routes on this measure. 21 The

number of habitable structures within 500 feet of route centerline ranges from 80 to 184 across the

122 filed routes.22 Route 894 impacts among the lowest number of habitable structures and well

below the midpoint of the overall range, with only 85 habitable structures within 500 feet of route

centerline.23

        This performance directly satisfies the Commission’s prudent avoidance standard: where

feasible alternatives exist, routes should not be drawn through or near occupied structures and

residences, and where routes are otherwise comparable the Commission should prefer the route

that places the fewest habitable structures in close proximity to the line. 24 In addition to Route

894’s other favorable criteria above, it performs very highly on avoiding habitable structures and

should thus be favored over otherwise comparable routes.


                III.     LINK J33 AND THE CAVALLINO AIRPORT CONFLICT

        Independent of Route 894’s affirmative merits, all routes utilizing Link J33 should be

rejected because they threaten a significant private aviation facility that the Joint Applicants’ EA

entirely failed to identify and evaluate.

        1. Link J33 Would Directly Interfere with Cavallino Airport Operations.

        The Cavallino Airport features a 4,500-foot runway located only approximately 5,600 feet

from the centerline of proposed Link J33.25 A 765-kV transmission line of the height contemplated

 in the Application placed this close to the runway directly threatens the approach and departure

corridors that pilots rely on to safely land and take off. 26 Structures of this scale in such proximity

would significantly constrain the categories of aircraft the Airport is designed to accommodate,

both now and in the future as the Airport expands to serve larger, multi-engine aircraft. 27

        The conflict is not merely operational. Mr. Jaffe has invested substantial capital in

developing the Cavallino Airport as a long-term infrastructure asset. 28 A 765-kV transmission

corridor running within 5,600 feet of the runway would impair his ability to expand or enhance

the Airport over the decades-long life of the line—creating permanent uncertainty about what

operational limitations the transmission infrastructure might impose as aviation regulations and

aircraft requirements evolve.29 Unlike some other affected property interests, an airport cannot

simply be relocated or reconfigured to avoid the conflict. 30

        2. Cavallino Airport Will Be a Private Airport of Regional Significance.

        The Cavallino Airport is not a speculative or nominal facility. It is under active ongoing

development by an experienced aviation business which owns and manages a portfolio of airports,

including one of the longest private airport runways in Texas. 31 The Jaffe family has owned and

operated Jetran—a leading aircraft leasing, sales, and services operation—for nearly four decades,

and Mr. Jaffe brings over fourteen years of experience managing diversified aviation businesses. 32

Aircraft commonly associated with Jetran and affiliate Spectre Air that would potentially fly in

 and out of the Cavallino Airport include passenger and freighter aircraft operating with

international flag carriers and entrepreneurial airlines worldwide. 33

         The Cavallino Airport received a Finding of No Objection from the FAA on June 5, 2026,

and the Airport will become operational upon completion of the active ongoing construction. 34

The fact that the Airport is not yet operational does not diminish its significance for purposes of

the Commission’s routing analysis. 35 It would be unreasonable to approve a route that is certain

to impair this FAA-recognized airport upon its imminent completion.

         3. The EA’s Failure to Account for the Cavallino Airport Renders the Analysis of
            Link J33 Routes Incomplete.

         Perhaps most critically, the Joint Applicants’ EA entirely failed to identify or evaluate the

Cavallino Airport when analyzing route alternatives.36 By failing to identify the Cavallino Airport,

the EA understates the impact of every route that utilizes Link J33. 37 As Mr. D’Andrea concluded,

all routes that include Link J33 should be treated as having one additional private airstrip conflict

beyond what is reported in the Application and EA.38

         This omission raises a broader concern about the completeness and reliability of the EA’s

private airstrip analysis more generally.39 If an active, FAA-studied private use airport undergoing

ongoing construction and less than two miles from a proposed link was missed entirely, the

 Commission cannot have confidence that the EA’s airstrip inventory for Link J33 or other

comparable links is accurate and complete. 40

        4. Route 894 Avoids the Cavallino Airport Conflict Entirely.

        Route 894 does not utilize Link J33 and therefore avoids the Cavallino Airport conflict

altogether.41 This is yet another independent, affirmative reason to prefer Route 894 over any

alternative that depends on Link J33. Where an otherwise favorable route avoids a conflict that

competing routes cannot, and where that conflict was entirely omitted from the environmental

analysis supporting those competing routes, the Commission should select that route.

                         IV.      CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION

        The record in this proceeding establishes that Route 894 achieves the best overall balance

across all applicable PURA and Commission routing criteria: it is near the shortest and least

expensive of the filed routes,42 parallels compatible existing ROW for nearly 44% of its length,43

and has among the fewest habitable structures in close proximity to its centerline. 44 No single

route excels on every criterion, but Route 894 performs well on the most important criteria without

material deficiencies on any.45

        Second, all routes utilizing Link J33 must be rejected because they would directly interfere

with the Cavallino Airport, a private aviation facility with FAA recognition and substantial capital

Attachment 11 at 5.

 investment which the Joint Applicants’ EA failed to identify or analyze. 46 That failure renders the

EA’s evaluation of Link J33 routes materially incomplete, and the Commission should not approve

a route whose impacts on the Airport were never studied.47 Route 894 avoids the Cavallino Airport

conflict entirely.48

        Considered holistically under the applicable statutory and regulatory framework, Route

894 is the appropriate route for the Commission to select.

                       IV.      CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION

        The record in this proceeding establishes that Route 894 achieves the best overall balance

across all applicable PURA and Commission routing criteria: it is near the shortest and least

expensive of the filed routes,42 parallels compatible existing ROW for nearly 44% of its length,43

and has among the fewest habitable structures in close proximity to its centerline. 44 No single

route excels on every criterion, but Route 894 performs well on the most important criteria without

material deficiencies on any.45
